full_judgment: 8. As to the defence case, the copy of a complaint petition accompanied with a medical certificate of the counter case has been given as part of examination of the accused under section 342 Cr PP PWs 1, 2 and 3 have also admitted that in the counter case they were the main accused. But what was the fate of the counter case, whether it was tried by the same court in accordance with the established procedure of trial of cross-cases, has not been mentioned in the judgment of either the trial Court or the appellate Court or the appellate Court. The procedure for trial of counter-cases by the same court is founded on a sound principle of Criminal trials Trial of cross-cases which arise from the same incident, by the same court enables it to better appreciate the evidence and circumstances which are described by parties in conflicting manners. By such trial the Court gets both sides of the picture and arrives at correct decision avoiding conflicting findings which are likely to occur if separate courts held the trials. Though no express provision of law requires trial of cross-cases by the same court. Practice and experience of over a century dictate such trial for arriving at correct determination of disputed facts. This is all the more necessary to save the accused from being prejudiced in their defence. In the instant case, it appears the counter case was not tried by the same court and as such the defence version of the case did not find due consideration from any of the courts below. Defence taken by the accused is that the complainant's party raided their house in any attempt to forcibly take away Santusti Begum where upon a suffice took place in which the deceased Nurul Islam received the fatal blow accidentally. They defence case need not be approved by examining witnesses; if some indication in their favour is available from cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses then this may be sufficient for their acquittal. The manner of the incident as alleged by the prosecution must be proved by the prosecution alone; that burden never shifts. If the manner of the incident is not proved, the prosecution must fail no matter the defence version of the case has not been proved either. Manner of the occurrence, according to the prosecution, is that while Nurul Islam was sleeping after having been nicely entertained with a dinner, he was treacherously attacked and killed on the chowki. But the Investigating Officer (PW 20) found the lungi of the victim put on in 'malkocha' fashion. A person while going to sleep does not put on 'malkocha.' A malkocha indicates preparation for facing impending assault, offensive or defensive. In the case of the deceased Nurul Islam there was no occasion for either as he was sleeping The 'malkocha: rather tends support to the defence case that Nurul Islam and his men forcibly entered the hut and tried to take away his estranged wife. Neither of the courts below applied its mind to this question, nor did they sift the evidence nor make critical analysis of it. Even glaring inconsistent statements of PW 1 vis-a-vis his ejahar on material Points escaped their notice. The First Information Report was lodged ten hours after the incident-whereas it could have been lodged within 3/4 hours at the best. But the trial Court observed that the First Information Report was lodged immediately after the occurrence. It is not only that the conviction of the accused persons was based on the uncorroborated testimony of a single witness, but also the facts and circumstances tend to show that the incident took place in different circumstances. If five assailants armed, as they were according to PW 1, has assaulted the victim simultaneously with" dagger and sharp daos" more than one injury would have been the result. Only one injury as found in the dead body negatives the evidence of PW 1 as a witness of truth. In these circumstances the accused are entitled to benefit of doubt.
